subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: API Key and Token Security
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: API Key and Token Security.

hook.text: A developer commits an API key to a public GitHub repo. Bots find it within minutes and start spending.

buildup.text: API keys and tokens are credentials. Exposing them gives attackers the same access you have.

discovery.text: Keys belong in environment variables or secret managers, never in source code or client bundles.

twist.text: Even private repos aren't safe. Former employees, leaked backups, and accidental forks spread secrets.

climax.text: Secret scanning in CI catches a key before it's committed. Automated rotation limits damage from old keys.

punchline.text: Treat API keys like passwords. Store them in secrets, not code.

quiz.question: Where should API keys be stored?
options: In source code for easy access
In environment variables or secret managers
